To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we report the expression, purification and crystallization of N-DCLK, a novel tandem of two doublecortin domains, and the successful crystallizaton of the N-domain.

the expression and purification protocol for the tandem and the isolated domains from human DCLK and the crystallization of the isolated N-terminal domain (residues Leu49-Ser154) were developed and that the crystals diffracted to a resolution of 1.5 and 1.8 A for the wild type and the SeMet-substitued form, respectively.
the tandem from human doublecortinet-like kinase was expressed in Escherichia coli as a fusion protein with maltose-binding protein and purified to homogeneity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first structural characterization of this unique tandem domain.
the structural characterization of the N-DCLK domain, which is the most conserved part of the tandem.
the structural analysis of the N-terminal doublecortin homology domain from DCLK.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is a very promising system for structure determination and for the study of the interaction of the tandem with tubulin/micrtobules.

the crystals of the N-terminal doublecortin tandem of DCLK are orthorhombic, with space group P2 (1) 2 (1)2 (1) and unit-cell parameters a= 37.5, b= 38.9, c= 41.1 A, alpha= 90, beta= 90, gamma= 90 degrees, with one molecule in the asymmetric unit.
the N-DCLK domain crystallizes in both space groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystallization of the isolated domains of DCLK has been achieved.
the N-terminal domain of DCLK can be expressed in Escherichia coli and can be crystallized.
the N-terminal domain of human DCLK is a good candidate for X-ray crystallographic studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tandem of doublecortin domains can be expressed and crystallized in the absence of the linker region.
the N-terminal tandem domain from DCLK is amenable to crystallization and can be a useful model for the study of microtubule interactions.

the crystallization of the tandem is hampered by the presence of the C-terminal domain, whereas the isolated N-terminal domain crystallizes easily and is a suitable starting point for structural studies.
